summary: The mac runner is unreachable, so all new work goes to the idle neo-ssd runner, which has the full 6 hours. The plan tests whether xs beats rsync on the local psample backup when both use eager writeback, and confirms xs if it wins. It also covers the 1% re-sync cell that LC4 never reported, and checks whether eager writeback combines with --no-atomic. Together these use about 352 of the 360 available minutes, counting the possible confirmation.

runners.rationale: The mac runner is unreachable and the evidence has no inventory for the mac host, so no experiment can be scheduled on mac-mars-10g this window. The open mac work (xs-recv4 follow-ups and the T13 pull onto the Mac) waits until it reports again.

rejected.reason: mac is not a running runner

runners.rationale: neo-ssd is idle with nothing queued, so it has 360 minutes; real-psample costs 8 minutes per sample. In LC3, rsync with eager writeback beat default xs, while xs-eager was much faster than xs. No experiment has put xs-eager against rsync-eager directly, and that comparison decides whether xs can beat rsync on this local copy. LC4 reported only the no-op cell, so the 1% update re-sync is still open. The eager plus --no-atomic combination has not been tried. The waiting tree confirmation of xs-eager against plain xs (LC3-durable-confirm) is left to the T14 tree, so it is not duplicated here. Budget: 96 minutes of screening plus 128 if the confirmation runs, then 64 and 64, about 352 minutes in total.

accepted.question: When both tools flush eagerly, does xs -aH get the psample backup safely onto the T5 sooner than rsync -aH?
After 1% of the psample files change, does xs -aH re-sync the local T5 backup faster than rsync -aH with cold caches?
Does skipping the temp-file rename add any speed on top of eager writeback for the local psample backup?
